correctness.rationale: All parameters and boundaries are explicit. The geometric fixed space is modeled by invariant edge orbits. The Cayley bipartiteness character criterion is proved, including disconnected components. Odd-order direct factors produce a simplicial retraction, not a homology-only comparison. For \(C_{2^a}\), two-adic valuations partition all admissible supports into a full simplex per valuation. For \(C_{2^a}\) x C2, the subgroup-projection dichotomy proves that precisely 2a+1 simplex facets cover the complex; their exact nonempty intersections yield a contractible nerve core plus a independent edges and thus a wedge of a circles. The complete proof is in RESULT.md, and verify.py directly tests real Cayley graph bipartiteness for exhaustive \(a\le4\) cases and multiple odd factors. Experiments are not used to establish the infinite assertion.

originality.rationale: For all \(a\ge2\) this is a new infinite non-elementary abelian two-group family relative to the checked claims. The ordinary t-colorability-complex theorems of Chari and Linusson-Shareshian do not determine geometric fixed spaces. Their mathematical statements are nonequivariant: ambient sphere-wedge dimension |A|-2 cannot imply fixed circle multiplicities or the odd-factor retraction. The existing elementary-abelian boundary case \(a=1\) does not imply the a-dependent nerve for \(a\ge2\). Cayley-bipartite graph enumeration does not imply a topological nerve theorem. Materially relevant full-text gaps remain a residual risk, not a proof of uniqueness.

value.rationale: A natural graph-property complex has fixed-point topology governed by the two-primary decomposition of its regular translation group. For each \(a\ge2\) the rank-one group has a disconnected a-component fixed space, while adjoining C2 produces a connected wedge of a circles, with unbounded free fundamental-group rank. Odd-order factors are shown homotopically irrelevant by a general simplicial reduction. This is a structural infinite-family classification with exact integral homotopy information, not a known-table recomputation, isolated finite sample, or routine parameter substitution.
